slides.headline: What makes a carousel readable
slides.emphasisLine: Four things, none of them design
slides.bodyText: The second example deck. This one uses the standard layout rather than the terminal one.

slides.headline: One idea per slide
slides.emphasisLine: If it needs a comma, it needs two slides
slides.bodyText: A slide is read in about a second and a half. Two ideas on one slide means one of them is skipped.

slides.headline: Front-load the headline
slides.emphasisLine: The first three words do the work
slides.bodyText: People decide whether to swipe from the top line alone. Everything below it is for the ones who already did.

slides.headline: Contrast beats decoration
slides.emphasisLine: It is read at thumbnail size first
slides.bodyText: Anything under 4.5:1 disappears in the feed. The checker flags it before you export.

slides.headline: Try changing something
slides.emphasisLine: Shift-click any control to apply it to every slide

captions.instagram:
Four things that decide whether a carousel gets read, and none of them are design choices.

One idea per slide. Front-load the headline. Contrast over decoration. Check it before you post.

This is an example deck included with Social Studio. Change it and watch the preview keep up.
captions.linkedin:
Four things that decide whether a carousel is read, none of which are design choices.

One idea per slide, because a slide gets about a second and a half. The headline front-loaded, because that is what the swipe decision is made on. Contrast over decoration, because it is seen at thumbnail size first.

An example deck included with Social Studio, an open source tool for building carousels, slideshows and Reels locally.
